reasons.plausibility: The role of Cu-rich precipitates in promoting a protective oxide scale and reducing wear at high temperature is plausible given known oxidation behaviors, though it is not fully certain that Cu is the primary controlling species compared to Cr or other elements.
reasons.testability: The proposed experiment—altering the Cu-rich phase fraction and comparing wear performance under controlled high-temperature sliding—is straightforward and gives a clear criterion for falsification.
reasons.usefulness: It directly addresses a key engineering challenge in high-entropy alloy coatings and provides a clear path to improving high-temperature wear performance by controlling microstructural features.
